title: Which class has the fewest girls?
description: A pictograph shows the girls in Classes 1 to 8, where one symbol stands for four girls and half a symbol for two. Multiplying the symbols by four gives each class, and then the least, a difference, a change in one row and the girls in Class 7 are found.
teaching_notes: One idea: read a pictograph by multiplying the number of symbols by what one symbol stands for, and a half symbol by half of that. Watch for students who count each symbol as one girl.

video_script.why: The child reads a pictograph whose symbol stands for four girls, with half symbols, and answers four questions from the counts.
video_script.substitution: The girls in each class are read from the symbols of a pictograph with a scale.
video_script.anchor: a pictograph of the girls in Classes 1 to 8, with one symbol for four girls and a half symbol for two girls
video_script.payoff_line: Class eight has the fewest girls, and Class seven has twelve girls

final_answer.value: a. Class 8; b. 6; c. the last half symbol becomes a full symbol; d. 12
final_answer.spoken: class eight has the fewest girls, the difference is six, the last half symbol becomes a full symbol, and class seven has twelve girls

maths_rules: key: 1 symbol = 4 girls, half symbol = 2 girls
girls in Class 1 to Class 8: 6 symbols = 24, 4 and a half = 18, 5 = 20, 3 and a half = 14, 2 and a half = 10, 4 = 16, 3 = 12, 1 and a half = 6
least is Class 8 with 6 girls (1 and a half symbols = 4 + 2)
Class 2: 18 + 2 = 20, which is 5 full symbols because 20 / 4 = 5, so the half symbol becomes a full symbol
check: counting by fours, 4, 8, 12 for Class 7; and 4 + 2 = 6 for Class 8
video_script.design: The pictograph of the book is read row by row using its scale. Each of the four questions is answered from the counted girls, and two answers are checked by counting in fours.
open_questions: The symbol counts of Classes 1, 3 and 4 (6, 5 and 3 and a half) come from the worklist, because the extracted book text does not show the figure. They match the girls 24, 20 and 14.

narration: <bookmark mark='mult'/>Step one, multiply the full symbols in each row by four.
<bookmark mark='one'/>Class one has six symbols, so six times four is twenty four. Class three has five, which makes twenty. Class six has four, which makes sixteen.
<bookmark mark='half'/>A half symbol adds two. Class two has sixteen and two, which is eighteen. Class four has twelve and two, which is fourteen.
<bookmark mark='more'/>Class five has eight and two, which is ten. Class eight has four and two, which is six.
<bookmark mark='rest'/>Class seven has three symbols, and three times four is twelve.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: the least is 6 girls, in Class 8

narration: <bookmark mark='compare'/>Step two, compare the eight counts.
<bookmark mark='small'/>The least is six girls, in Class eight.

narration: <bookmark mark='add'/>Step four, Class two has eighteen girls. Two more girls make twenty.
<bookmark mark='full'/>Twenty is five times four, so the half symbol becomes a full symbol.

<bookmark mark='half'/>For Class eight, four and a half symbol of two make six.
